target_customer: Mobile game and app developers with existing iOS Objective-C or C++ code who wanted Android versions
problem: Porting an iOS app to Android meant maintaining a separate Java codebase. Apportable let developers cross-compile Objective-C apps to Android.
business_model: Developer tooling (SDK and porting service), later enterprise offering Tengu

founders.name: Collin Jackson
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by VentureBeat (2016); background not found in sources I opened.

founders.name: Ian Fischer
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by VentureBeat (2016); background not found.

exit.reason: Acqui-hire: Google quietly hired the founders and 11 other engineers and later reports said the rest of the staff of about 65 were let go

technical_complexity.rationale: Cross-compiling Objective-C and the iOS framework APIs to run on Android is a compiler and runtime engineering problem that required reimplementing large parts of Cocoa.

defensibility.rationale: Hard to replicate technically, but dependent on Apple and Google platform rules and APIs that could change.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google bought the team in 2015 and Tengu and other products were discontinued.

market_need_then: Popular iOS games such as Kingdom Rush and Osmos used it to reach Android stores, and the 2013 seed round was framed around automatically converting iOS games to Android.

brand_strength.rationale: A search for brand story returned nothing about the company; only developer-community recognition via the games that used it.

outcome_analysis: Apportable solved a hard compiler problem and raised about $7.4M, including a 2013 seed from Google Ventures, but VentureBeat reported sources saying it had financial difficulties before Google quietly acqui-hired the founders and a few engineers in 2015, with most staff let go and products shut down. It fits an acquihire soft landing for a platform dependent tool.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503; YC page lists no founders. The February 2014 $5M round is from outlet headlines and snippets (pocketgamer.biz, vcpost, finsmes); investors listed from a snippet, and ZoomInfo attributes the lead to Initialized Capital, a conflict. Stage labeled other because sources do not state it (Seedtable calls it Series A). Total of $7.4M per VentureBeat. Acquisition believed March 2015 with founders joining May 2015 per VentureBeat. Dated 2011 competitor sources (Xamarin and Marmalade existed, Mono blog 2011) were not clearly tied to Apportable, so the list is empty.
